text:
Exact-item recurrence depends on preprocessing, not the Amazon category name. The official [Amazon Reviews 2023 benchmark scripts](https://github.com/hyp1231/AmazonReviews2023/blob/main/benchmark_scripts/README.md) retain only the earliest interaction per user–item pair; consequently, exact-item repeats and held-out target recurrence are zero after this transformation. Removing duplicate records with identical timestamps is weaker and can preserve later repeats. Deduplication also changes sequence lengths, recency and potentially k-core membership. Measure per-category repeat-user coverage and repeated-event counts in the actual model-visible training histories; report zero eligible users as unavailable evidence, not zero model dependence. Semantic repeated interests across distinct items require a separately defined title/description similarity proxy.

Deletion-based explanations measure recommendation changes after removing history evidence; [counterfactual evaluation research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.01310) provides this general framework. [Missing-input experiments](https://iris.uniroma1.it/bitstream/11573/1740238/1/Siciliano_Robust-Training_2024.pdf) show sequential recommenders can depend strongly on recent interactions. For this benchmark, a proposed controlled design is paired validation evaluation: recent-history or repeated-interest removal versus multiple random controls matched on removal count, original history length, recency distribution and contiguous-block structure. Keep users, targets and candidate sets fixed; report macro HR@10 changes, target-rank changes and paired uncertainty.

To separate content dependence from positional effects, compare ordinary deletion/repacking with an intervention preserving surviving items’ original absolute position IDs and correctly masking removed tokens; neither intervention is artifact-free. For overlapping recent/repeated sets, evaluate each set, their intersection, exclusive portions and union; never sum deletion effects. Stratify by retained length and removal fraction, exclude empty histories, and compare plausible same-length histories or supported replacements. These controls are methodological recommendations: shortened or internally masked histories may be out of distribution, so perturbation sensitivity alone does not establish causal preference dependence.
